plain.li: [opt0] Frost coming. All hands out with baskets until dark. Backs aching, cellar full.
[opt1] Two helpers and the best baskets. We got the seed plants in. Not much else.
[opt2] Frost last night, like I said. Walked the rows this morning. Black, all of it.
[opt0] We picked by torchlight with frost already on the baskets. Got most of what was ripe.

warm.li: [opt0] They all came out to the fields when I asked. I didn't even have to ask twice.

blunt.li: [opt2] Told them it would freeze. It froze.

cheerful.li: [opt0] Raced the frost and won, mostly! The cellar smells like summer.

gloomy.li: [opt2] All that work since spring, gone in one clear night.

cold.li: [opt1] Saved the seed stock and the herbs. The rest was a fair price for the hours.

plain.li: [opt0] Sat up by the pens all night with a lamp. Eyes past the lamplight near dawn, then nothing.
[opt1] The herd goes in every night now. The barn smells like it.
[opt2,safe] The tracks stopped coming. Whatever it was went somewhere easier.
[opt2,risk] Gap under the gate this morning, and one of them gone. I counted three times.

warm.li: [opt0] Kept watch over the animals all night. They settled once they saw the lamp.

blunt.li: [opt2,risk] Should have watched the pens. Didn't. Now one's gone.

cheerful.li: [opt0] Threw a stick at a pair of eyes and they ran off. Best throw I've ever made.

gloomy.li: [opt2] Lay awake listening for the herd. Every sound was teeth.

cold.li: [opt1] Moving the herd in at night costs an hour a day. Cheaper than replacing them.

plain.li: [opt0] Word came about {TALE}. Dead, months ago. We held a wake tonight and I talked too much.
[opt1] The council gave me the day. I walked as far as the river and back.
[opt3] Heard about {TALE}. Went back to work. Didn't say anything.
[opt0] Told them all about {TALE}. Somebody poured an extra cup.
[opt1] Walked all day. Didn't think about much. Then I thought about everything.
[opt2] Planted a tree for {TALE} out past the last row of the fields. Put a stone by it. Watered it twice.

warm.li: [opt0] They listened to every story. I didn't know how much I needed someone to listen.
[opt2] There's a sapling by the fields now with a stone beside it. I'll sit there when I need to.

blunt.li: [opt3] Somebody I knew died. Work still needs doing.

cheerful.li: [opt0] We laughed more than we cried at the wake. That would have pleased them.

gloomy.li: [opt3] Gone, and buried, and I wasn't there. I wasn't there.

cold.li: [opt3] Word came: {TALE} is dead. It was a long time ago, and far away.

plain.li: [opt0] Found {TALE} on a trader's blanket today. Bought it back. It's on the shelf over my bed.
[opt1,safe] Got {TALE} back for half the price. I owe somebody a drink.
[opt1,risk] The haggling went wrong and {TALE} went back in the trader's pack. Gone again.
[opt2,safe] Told the trader it was stolen. The trader looked at me and handed it over.
[opt3] Saw {TALE} for sale today. Put it back down. Someone else has it now.

warm.li: [opt0] The council paid for {TALE}. I didn't ask them to. I'll remember it.

blunt.li: [opt2,risk] Called the trader a thief. The trader left. So did {TALE}.

cheerful.li: [opt0] It's back! Scratch on the back and all.

gloomy.li: [opt3] The one thing left from before, and I watched someone else carry it off.

cold.li: [opt3] An object. I don't need it to remember.

plain.li: [opt0] Wrote home to say I'm staying. Sealed it before I could change my mind.
[opt1] The colony sent silver home for {TALE}. A long letter went with it, most of it mine.
[opt0] They wanted me home for {TALE}. I said no. I'm needed here.

warm.li: [opt1] The council sent my family silver without being asked twice. I'll pay it back in work.

blunt.li: [opt0] They'll manage without me. They'll have to.

cheerful.li: [opt1] The silver will hire two good hands at home. Better than one of me!

gloomy.li: [opt0] Chose this place over my own people. I'd choose it again, and I don't feel good about that.

cold.li: [opt0] Answered the letter from home. The colony has the better claim on my time.

plain.li: [opt0,safe] Games with the traveler until late. We came out ahead.
[opt0,risk] Games with the traveler until late. Purses lighter in the morning. No idea how.
[opt1,safe] Played the gambler for the colony's stake and won it on the last game.
[opt1,risk] Played the gambler for the colony's stake and lost. Watched every move. Still lost.
[opt2] A gambler came through. The council said no games. I'd have liked to see how good they were.

warm.li: [opt0] Loud night round the table. I haven't laughed like that in a while.

blunt.li: [opt1,risk] Lost. Don't want to talk about it.

cheerful.li: [opt1,safe] Beat a professional at their own game!

gloomy.li: [opt1,risk] They all watched me lose the stake. I'll hear about it all winter.

cold.li: [opt1] The gambler's odds were good. Mine were better, or worse. Chance either way.
